LESSON: PLANTS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Resources in our Environment
Topic 3.2: Plants
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Plants, part of Resources in our Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we care for plants?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify ways of caring for plants using locally available materials,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plants in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. carry out activities for caring of plants using locally available materials,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plants in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. Advocate for plant protection for environmental sustainability. ● Learners with low vision observe pictures, photographs or watch video clips of people watering, manuring and mulching plants. Learners with blindness listen to clear verbal descriptions of pictures, photographs or audio clips of people watering, manuring and mulching plants. ● Learners are guided to water, manure and do mulching for some plants in the school compound. ● Learners with low vision observe pictures, photographs or video clips of healthy plants that have been conserved. Learners with blindness listen to audio clips or picture descriptions of healthy plants that have been conserved. ● Learners are guided to write plant protection messages by hand, electronic, print or braille resources, recite poems and sing songs on plant protection. How can we care for plants?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plants in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Plants together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: learner develops originality when creating plant protection messages using own hand writings, electronic print or

braille resources.

Values:
Responsibility: learner develops self-driven skills when writing plant protection messages by hand, electronic, print or braille resources.

22

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: learner develops environmental education and climate change skills when watering, manuring and mulching plants in the school

compound.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Messages on plant protection relates to writing skills in Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Approved support learning materials, local environment, flash cards, braille cards, pictures, digital devices with assistive technology, watering

cans, manure, dry grass or leaves.
